summary: The selected 0.32.3 publisher (release.yml publish-packages) records about 191 events across the pre-writer census and both feed loops. Before this change, each --record-event call under FSGG_RELEASE_ATTEMPT=0323 re-ran native settlement authentication: six GITHUB_TOKEN requests, including an archive download. That is about 1,150 requests against the 1,000/h per-repository GITHUB_TOKEN limit (non-Enterprise), shared with other workflows, and they would fall inside irreversible push loops under set -e. Unit tests mocked accepted_tag_settlement on the record path, so the request count was never exercised; independent dispatch review found it. Records now use verified_cached_tag_settlement with zero transport. It joins the cached receipt bytes to the selected receiptSha256, this attempt's input-binding coordinates and the shared receipt claims. The static guard and acquisition still authenticate natively once. Lesson: count repeated per-event side calls in effect loops with real (non-mocked) callees and transport counters, not only by contract tests. Related: after settlement creates the tags, the preflight-only route refuses existing tags, so post-settlement eligibility is established only inside the publish job before its first writer. This records source behaviour only, not hosted publication or rate-limit measurement.
title: Publisher event records must not re-authenticate the settlement over the network
